A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RGB-Thermal grounding benchmark and RGBT-VGNet baseline, renamed RGBT-GroundBench in v2. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark statistics, grounding experiments, fine-grained evaluations, qualitative comparisons, and AMA/LAVS ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original evaluations and reports additional grounding baselines, MLLM experiments, fusion comparisons, rank ablations, and annotation-quality outcomes.

M1.justification: V2 adds Tri-Prior Fusion (TPF), combining illumination, local semantic, and global semantic priors to weight RGB/TIR features. Fused visual tokens replace the separate RGB/TIR token inputs to the grounding transformer. AMA and LAVS are retained; TPF is a substantive new computational component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate bounding-box grounding on RefFLIR, RefM3FD, and RefMFAD, retaining the same modalities and environmental categories. New model, resolution, and metric experiments reuse this coverage. The revised counting, segmentation, VQA, and captioning discussions describe potential extensions, not additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds FSVG and AttBalance, including their multimodal variants, to the main and fine-grained comparisons. It also evaluates Naive Add, CMX, and LIF fusion alternatives and five MLLMs: GLM-4.6V, GLM-4.6V-Flash, Kimi-K2.5, Qwen3.5-Plus, and Qwen3-VL-Plus. Earlier grounding comparators are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds Acc@0.7 evaluation, MLLM tests at 224x224 and original resolution, and equal-total-rank controls. It also revises reported TestC counts from 5,384 to 5,360 and names Qwen3-VL instead of Qwen-VL for captioning; these disclosures do not establish that all annotations or experiments were regenerated. The original 120-epoch training budget remains.

E4.justification: The existing AMA/LAVS ablation becomes v2 Table 5 with an additional TPF configuration. New Tables 6 and 10 compare fusion strategies and symmetric versus asymmetric LoRA allocations. Sections 7.1-7.2 additionally examine localization-threshold sensitivity and MLLM resolution/modality sensitivity, substantially extending the earlier diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2 acknowledges possible MLLM response variability but introduces no corresponding statistical estimation or uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive baseline, fusion, rank, Acc@0.7, and MLLM results. With the revised full model, main-table test Acc@0.5 entries change from 72.65/74.34/66.63 to 72.43/74.89/67.58 for RefFLIR/RefM3FD/RefMFAD; this is not a uniform gain. Fine-grained RGBT-VGNet entries also change. Table 1 revises weak-light instances from 8,971 to 16,726 and small objects from 22,831 to 22,009.

T1.justification: Section 4 adds mathematical definitions for TPF's illumination quality, local/global gates, reliability weights, and fused tokens, including Equations 8-10. Existing AMA/LAVS mathematics remains essentially unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 reorganizes the main contributions around the benchmark, empirical findings, and a reference baseline, with the unified framework explicitly treated as benchmark infrastructure. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add claims about LoRA robustness and MLLM cross-spectral limitations, and describe the new TPF component.

C2.justification: V2 interprets MLLM fusion benefits as dependent on model and resolution, qualifies service-based rankings, and explains why moderate LoRA asymmetry balances thermal adaptation against RGB semantics. It also adds explicit remaining failures involving small, occluded, or ambiguous targets and removes v1's extended justification for omitting a LAVS-only ablation.

D1.justification: V1 promises a future release; v2 supplies code and dataset links and states that annotations, splits, checkpoints, and evaluation scripts are released, with licensing information. V2 also discloses annotation acceptance criteria and review/edit/removal rates, the selected AMA ranks of 16/48, and TPF preprocessing details. External availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Related work expands to FSVG, AttBalance, and frozen-MLLM attention approaches such as F-LMM and Localization Head, alongside updated RGB-T references. Some introductory benchmark citations, including Cops-ref and MC-Bench, are removed. The central positioning of RGB-T grounding as underexplored remains.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the benchmark, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contribution statement, and conclusion. It integrates the framework into the evaluation protocol, moves component ablation into the main text, reorganizes the supplement into numbered sections, and extensively rewrites appendix lists as connected prose.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the two-column layout with a single-column format, merges v1 Tables 4-5 into Table 4, adds several experimental tables, and places fine-grained tables alongside their discussion. Figure 4 adds TPF and Figure 1 updates the model comparison. Existing qualitative image panels are retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation through equal-budget rank controls, alternative fusion comparisons, stricter localization evaluation, MLLM sensitivity tests, and quantified annotation-quality checks. These address important evidential gaps in v1, while concrete resource information improves reproducibility. Some new summaries disagree with their tables, notably Section 7.1's accuracy-drop calculations, but these reporting defects do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and transparency.
